newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bulgarian premier sees decline in inflation.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian premier sees decline in inflation.

text.p: Bulgarian Prime Minister Ivan Kostov, on his first international visit since taking office, said on Tuesday he expected a sharp decline in the country's inflation rate for the rest of 1997.
"By the end of the year we expect a sharp decline, so much so that for the rest of the year inflation should not exceed two percentage points per month," he told reporters.
At the end of April Bulgaria's consumer price inflation stood at 1,965.3 percent, year-on-year.
Kostov said that for this month "We expect the figure to be close to zero or very small."
Earlier, he met European Union's External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek in a bid to push his country's EU membership bid.

Van den Broek told reporters that the economic and political reform plans unveiled by Kostov had "given a certain sense of optimism" as the Commission finalises advice to EU governments on Bulgaria's application to join the bloc.
The Commission is working on a report due on July 15 on all 10 central and east European countries in the queue for membership.
Bulgaria is not expected to be among the first to join in the first enlargement wave of either the EU or the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.

Kostov said he believed the budget plan he has presented will be endorsed by Bulgaria's parliament by the end of this month, and that deals with the World Bank and the International Monetary fund will be finalised, allowing EU macroeconomic assistance of 250 million ecus ($280 million) to be released.
It was Kostov's first visit abroad since taking office on May 21 after his Union of Democratic Forces swept to victory in April 19 general elections.
